comments.body: `get_pager_file` wraps `stream.buffer` in a new `MaybeStripAnsi(io.TextIOWrapper)` whenever the yielded stream is a real TextIO. When that temporary wrapper is garbage-collected, `TextIOWrapper.__del__` calls `close()`, which closes the underlying buffer. In the `_nullpager` path the buffer is `sys.stdout.buffer`, so the process's stdout is closed after any non-TTY `echo_via_pager` call. The same applies to `_pipepager`, where `stdin` is also wrapped and the original `c.stdin` is later closed. The PR-head test run supports this: 189 errors, many of them `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file` in unrelated tests that print after a pager test has run. The change should not create a second owner for a buffer that something else still owns (detach the original wrapper, or write through the existing text stream and strip ANSI manually instead of wrapping `.buffer`).

from click import echo_via_pager

def test_pager_does_not_close_stdout(monkeypatch):
    buf = io.BytesIO()
    fake = io.TextIOWrapper(buf, encoding='utf-8')
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, 'stdout', fake)
    monkeypatch.setattr(sys, 'stdin', io.TextIOWrapper(io.BytesIO()))
    monkeypatch.setenv('PAGER', '')
    monkeypatch.setenv('TERM', 'dumb')
    echo_via_pager('hello')
    import gc; gc.collect()
    assert not fake.closed and not buf.closed
    print('still usable', file=fake)
    fake.flush()

comments.body: Security defect in `_mask_hidden_input`. The raw-value pass uses `(?<!\w)...(?!\w)` lookarounds, so the secret is left unmasked whenever it is directly adjacent to a word character in the message. Example: a custom type that does `self.fail(f"bad{value}", ...)` with value `pass` produces `badpass`, and the lookbehind sees `d`, so nothing is masked and the password is echoed. The same happens for any value that starts or ends with a non-word character (e.g. `-secret` inside `a-secret`, or `!x` inside `q!x`). Before this change, the code fell back to a generic message whenever the value was not cleanly found, so it did not leak in these cases. Masking must not depend on word boundaries when the goal is to hide the input. Mask every occurrence of the raw value (or at least every occurrence that is not a whole-word mismatch of a different token), and do not let surrounding characters decide whether a secret is masked. Also, the new test `test_hide_input_value_never_leaks_when_err_true` passes `mix_stderr=False` to `runner.invoke`. That keyword was removed in Click 8.2, so this test may raise TypeError, and the suite reports 1 failed at the PR head. That failure is not explained by the diff, and the change must not merge with an unexplained failure in its own test file.

The rewrite drops the `self.allow_dash` condition. The original was `self.file_okay and self.allow_dash and rv in (b"-", "-")`, so `-` was only special when dash was allowed. Now `is_dash` is true for `-` whenever `file_okay` is set, even with `allow_dash=False`. Because the existence, stat and resolve checks run under `if not is_dash:`, `click.Path(exists=True, allow_dash=False).convert("-", None, None)` returns `"-"` without checking the filesystem, instead of failing with BadParameter. This is a behavior regression. Restore the `self.allow_dash` check, e.g. `is_dash = self.file_okay and self.allow_dash and rv == dash`. The new test only covers `allow_dash=True`, so it does not catch this.

comments.body: `_NamedTextIOWrapper.fileno()` now returns the host process's original fd (fd 1/2) when one was captured. Python-level callers that use the fd directly (`os.write(sys.stdout.fileno(), ...)`, `subprocess` with `stdout=sys.stdout`) will write to the real process stdout and bypass the `CliRunner` capture buffer, so `result.output` will not contain that output. This is a semantic change to a public-ish surface, and the PR gives no test showing that such writes are either captured or intentionally escaped. A human should confirm this is the intended tradeoff.

`test_faulthandler_enable` calls `faulthandler.enable()` and never calls `faulthandler.disable()`. The handler stays registered for the rest of the pytest process and points at the fd captured from the outer stderr, which pytest may close or reuse later. Consider a try/finally that disables faulthandler, or a monkeypatch around `faulthandler.enable`.

`_safe_fileno` catches only `AttributeError` and `io.UnsupportedOperation`. A stream that is already closed raises `ValueError` from `fileno()`, which would now propagate out of `invoke` before the isolation block starts. Whether that case is reachable should be checked before merging.

comments.body: This changes type inference for every Option with a non-basic flag_value and no explicit type. Such options previously got STRING and now get UNPROCESSED. That is a user-visible change to default and flag output for existing callers, not a bug fix. Two cases need a human decision. comments.body: The change alters documented default-resolution behavior for boolean flags. `{type: bool, default: True, flag_value: False}` used to resolve to False and now resolves to True, and existing expectations in test_options.py and test_termui.py were edited to match. The stated rationale (issue #3111 and a versionchanged note) is plausible but not verifiable from the diff. This file has a recent history of reverted sentinel changes, and the removed comment about callable flag_values (issue #3121) is no longer adjacent to the code it protected. The non-bool sentinel path, which still resolves `default=True` to `flag_value`, is the part most likely to regress, and I have not probed it. A human should confirm the intended semantics and check downstream users of `--x/--no-x` with `default=True` before this ships.

The pager fallback chain was removed. `_pager_contextmanager` now returns the first candidate's context manager directly. If `PAGER` is set but the command is missing, `_pipepager` yields `(stdout, 'utf-8', False)` and returns, so the `more`/`less`/nullpager fallbacks are never tried. The old code fell through to them. This is a behavior regression for `echo_via_pager` and `get_pager_file`.

The PR head test run is red: 1 failed and 189 errors, all in tests/test_utils.py, with `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`. This points to the new stream plumbing. Likely causes are `get_pager_file`'s `finally: stream.flush()` and the `MaybeStripAnsi(stream.buffer, ...)` wrapping, which can close or flush a stream the caller still uses. The regression must be fixed before this can merge.

`should_strip_ansi` now returns True for any stream that has a `color` attribute, without checking `color` or whether the stream is a tty. Any user object with a `color` attribute will have ANSI output stripped unconditionally. The check is also tied to the new `MaybeStripAnsi` wrapper, but it matches on attribute name alone. This is an overly broad condition.

`MaybeStripAnsi.write` strips ANSI only when `self.color` is falsy, and `color` may still be None at this point. The `None` default is never normalized to a bool before reaching this class on every path. The class also subclasses `TextIOWrapper` but does not handle `encoding`/`errors` consistently with the callers that pass `encoding=encoding`, so the wrapper's behavior is not verified.

`_tempfilepager` writes to a `NamedTemporaryFile` and then calls `subprocess.call`. The old `except OSError` for a missing command was removed. Any `OSError` from the pager launch now escapes, which is a regression for callers that relied on silent fallback.

comments.body: The PR-head run exits 1 with 1 failed and 189 errors, and the output does not name the failing test. The errors are `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file` in tests/test_utils.py, which this diff does not touch, so they may be pre-existing or caused by stream handling in the new tests. The new test `test_hide_input_value_never_leaks_when_err_true` calls `runner.invoke(..., mix_stderr=False)`. That keyword was removed in Click 8.2, so this may be the failure. Confirm which test fails and why before merging.

`_mask_hidden_input` only masks a raw value at word boundaries. A password that appears as a substring of a longer word in the error message (for example `bad` inside `badness`) is now shown unmasked, while the old code fell back to a generic message in that case. This is a partial leak of the secret and should be stated in the change or covered by a test. Also, when the value is `***`, the raw pass can rewrite the mask itself, producing a mangled message.

The message format changed from `"Error: {msg}"` / `"Error: {e.message}"` to `"Error: {message}"`. Existing translation catalogues keyed on the old msgids will no longer match, so localized users will see English errors. This should be confirmed against the #2902 localisation work.

comments.body: `_mask_hidden_input` does not skip the empty string, though its docstring says it does. For `value == ""`, `repr(value)` is `"''"`, which is harmless. But `if value is not None:` is true, so `re.sub(r"(?<!\w)(?!\w)", ...)` matches at every non-word boundary and inserts `'***'` throughout the message. For example, `_mask_hidden_input("too short", "")` returns a mangled string instead of `"too short"`. This path is reachable when a prompt has `default=""` and `hide_input=True` and `value_proc` raises a `UsageError`. The fix is to guard with `if value:` (or `if value is not None and value != ""`) so the empty value is skipped as documented. Add a regression test for the empty-value case.

`get_pager_file` wraps `stream.buffer` in a new `MaybeStripAnsi(io.TextIOWrapper)` and never detaches it. When that wrapper is garbage-collected, `TextIOWrapper.__del__` calls `close()`, which closes the underlying buffer. For the non-tty/nullpager path, `stream` is `sys.stdout` itself, so the process's real stdout buffer gets closed after `echo_via_pager` returns. The PR's own test run shows the symptom: 189 errors and 1 failure in tests/test_utils.py with `ValueError: I/O operation on closed file`, which is the cascade you get once stdout is closed. The same wrapping also means the original `c.stdin` TextIOWrapper in `_pipepager` and the new wrapper both write to one buffer, so buffered text can be reordered or lost. Fix by not closing the buffer on wrapper GC (e.g. wrap with `detach()` on exit or write through the original stream instead of creating a second TextIOWrapper), and make the test suite green before re-submitting.
